q: What records must a green hydrogen plant keep for certification in India?
title: Green hydrogen plant records to keep
short: Daily records of hydrogen output, its physical and chemical parameters and energy use by source, plus water, feedstock and losses, kept for at least five evaluation cycles. A monitoring plan must set out emission sources, instruments, calibration, data control and factors for the verification agency.
audience: Plant managers and EHS teams at green hydrogen facilities

ul: Hydrogen produced, with its physical and chemical parameters.
Energy consumed from each source, both aggregated and broken down.
Fuel and electricity consumption in detail.
Water consumption, feedstock consumption and losses.
Sales up to the first purchaser, or captive use, and whether the hydrogen was converted into a carrier.

p: GHCI calls it the Green Hydrogen MRV framework. It must cover:
ul: Emission source streams and activity data.
Monitoring instruments and how often they are calibrated.
Calibration of all critical instruments by certifying agencies.

p: At least five evaluation cycles, or since the start of operations if the plant is younger. MNRE or its agency may run random or sample audits during or after the year.

ul: PPAs and load dispatch centre certificates showing generation against consumption.
Green tariff bills and power exchange records.
Storage and banking records where renewable power was stored or banked.

p: Offtake data is kept for record only and does not affect the certificate. The verification agency may not insist on sensitive commercial data such as offtake contracts.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills, including green tariff bills, and fuel invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record, so the energy side of these files stays easy to find years later. Metered production data stays in your plant systems.
